rituals.name: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
rituals.unique_game_move: State Belief → Picture Outcome → Pay Out
rituals.recognition_cue: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.immediate_need: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.match_reason: Unexamined belief · Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.goal: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.steps:
1. State Belief — State the belief as a clear prediction.
2. Choose Safe — Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
3. Picture Outcome — Hold the expected result before acting.
4. Test Observation — Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
5. Pay Out — Pay out only to evidence.
rituals.win: ✓ Evidence won the bet. Belief did not get a sympathy payout.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Evidence won the bet. Belief did not get a sympathy payout.
rituals.tips:
• Let the present moment carry more weight than rigid certainty.
• One step toward freedom is enough for this round.
• An old label can soften without being argued away.
• Choose new evidence; your mind can update later.
• Make space for freedom before asking for certainty.

rituals.name: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.unique_game_move: Name → Remain Version → Climb Stair
rituals.recognition_cue: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.immediate_need: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.goal: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.steps:
1. Name — Name five versions of the task from almost easy to really stretching.
2. Cross Out — Remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Remain Version — Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Climb Stair — Next time, climb only one stair.
rituals.win: ✓ One stair was enough to create movement.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One stair was enough to create movement.
rituals.tips:
• Choose a smaller beginning while the mind is still asking for more.
• Choose a smaller beginning; your system does not need more pressure.
• Let a tiny start be practical rather than perfect.
• One useful choice can matter more than another round of delay.
• Let the next minute be about momentum, not overplanning.

rituals.name: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Activity → Add Sentence → Try Three Ways
rituals.recognition_cue: Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.immediate_need: Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.match_reason: Emotion–fact confusion · Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.goal: Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Activity — Choose one activity.
2. Score Expected — Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add Sentence — Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Try Three Ways — Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’
rituals.win: ✓ The feeling kept its voice but lost the judge’s chair.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The feeling kept its voice but lost the judge’s chair.
rituals.tips:
• Protect perspective by making the next decision smaller.
• Emotional weather is real; emotional obedience is still optional.
• Use a wider view to make the next hour kinder.
• Keep a calmer check available; emotional weather may not stay this loud.
• Keep balance protected while an intense emotion finds its level.

rituals.name: TWO ENGINES
rituals.unique_game_move: Schedule Chosen → Check Both → Drop Demand
rituals.recognition_cue: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.immediate_need: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.steps:
1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything.
rituals.win: ✓ Good-enough became usable again.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Good-enough became usable again.
rituals.tips:
• Use a smaller beginning before turning the stuck feeling into a life rule.
• Let starting pressure remain unfinished while you choose one doable move.
• The delay can be uncomfortable without being unmanageable.
• Notice the delay, but do not build your whole day around it.
• Let the stuck feeling be heard, then return to a sense of progress.

rituals.immediate_need: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.

PLAY TIME

45–60 seconds

GOAL

A crutch can hide the safety already holding you.

1. Identify Protective — During a manageable practice round, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying extra certainty.
2. Drop Legitimate — Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.

WIN

✓ Pressure separated from importance.

TIPS

• Keep a sense of progress visible when starting pressure gets loud.
• Keep a sense of progress protected while the delay finds its level.
• Removing one crutch can reveal strength that avoidance kept hidden.
• Let a tiny start reduce the pressure that the stuck feeling creates.
• Do not use overplanning as proof that the delay is correct.

MIND BEND

At the low tile, avoidance reinforcement can be a real feeling without becoming a proven conclusion.

FORMULA FLOW

Identify Protective → Drop Legitimate → Observe Outcome

SAFETY

PAUSE
Never remove medically required or genuinely protective behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
rituals.unique_game_move: Select Triggers → Drop Unnecessary → Stay Long
rituals.recognition_cue: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
rituals.immediate_need: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
rituals.match_reason: Automatic-pattern blindness · Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
rituals.goal: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.

1. Select Triggers — Select two triggers already manageable separately.
2. Predict Joining — Predict what joining them will add.
3. Drop Unnecessary — Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
4. Stay Long — Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.

• Keep choice visible when the habit pull gets loud.
• Stay close to a new pathway when mindless repetition feels tempting.

rituals.recognition_cue: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.
rituals.immediate_need: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.

PLAY TIME

about 1 minute

GOAL

Power may be expressed without becoming a weapon.

1. Create Space — Picture a private inner space where the anger can be named safely.
2. State Anger — State the anger plainly without rehearsing violence or revenge.
3. Find Boundary — Name the boundary, need, or value underneath the heat.
4. Choose Safe Action — Select one action that protects the boundary without causing damage.

WIN

✓ Anger kept its power and lost its weapon.

TIPS

• Clear limits prevent generosity from quietly turning into depletion.
• A calm no can protect both honesty and connection.
• Let space remain possible even if outside pressure stays.
• Keep fairness steady while over-responsibility moves through.
• A blurred boundary can be present while self-respect stays possible.

MIND BEND

Look through the single lantern: boundary confusion can predict a future it has never actually seen.

FORMULA FLOW

Create Space → State Anger → Find Boundary → Choose Safe Action

SAFETY

PAUSE
Leave immediately and get help if there is risk of harming anyone or damaging property.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
rituals.unique_game_move: Count Usable → Place Buffers → Start Earliest
rituals.recognition_cue: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
rituals.immediate_need: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
rituals.match_reason: Time-pressure distortion · Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
rituals.goal: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
rituals.unique_game_move: Name Causes → Describe Geometry → Choose Smallest
rituals.recognition_cue: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.
rituals.immediate_need: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.
rituals.match_reason: Emotion–fact confusion · Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.
rituals.goal: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.

2. Describe Geometry — Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
3. Choose Smallest — At the bell, choose the smallest Name that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.

• Do not let a strong feeling decide what you deserve.

rituals.name: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
rituals.unique_game_move: Set Brief → Attend Direct → Let Sensory
rituals.recognition_cue: Reality gets one minute without explanation.
rituals.immediate_need: Reality gets one minute without explanation.
rituals.match_reason: Sensory disconnection · Reality gets one minute without explanation.
rituals.goal: Reality gets one minute without explanation.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Brief — Set a brief interval.
2. Name Comparisons — During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
3. Attend Direct — Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
4. Let Sensory — If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.

rituals.ritualText:
KEEP ONE BRIDGE OPEN

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

Use this reset to start before motivation arrives—while keeping the next step visible.

1. Touch the task — Open the task and make one tiny mark. Leave the rest alone.
2. Choose one inch — Pick the smallest action you can finish quickly. No perfect feeling is needed.
3. Try one quick round — Give the chosen action a single focused pass. Use what is visible.
4. Stop at proof — Pause when you can see evidence that you started. Finish before adding more.
5. Leave a doorway — Set up the easiest next action before stepping away. Keep your hands slow.

WIN

✓ You changed the next minute and made a visible start while the old pattern was still present.

TIPS

• For motivation dependency, change one visible thing at a time.
• Choose visible proof over a perfect mood.
• Keep the first round shorter than your resistance.
• Make the first move physical, not theoretical.
• Stop planning when a usable doorway appears.

MIND BEND

Starting can create motivation; it does not have to wait for it. Touch the task → Try one quick round → Leave a doorway: Action can begin before the feeling changes.

FORMULA FLOW

Touch the task → Choose one inch → Try one quick round → Stop at proof → Leave a doorway

SAFETY

PAUSE
Stop if the exercise increases agitation or if the task involves immediate safety, medical, legal, or emergency decisions requiring qualified help.

rituals.challenge: Getting pulled away every few minutes in the moment

rituals.goal: bring your attention back to one target—with one small action.
rituals.steps:
1. Reset the screen — Move every unrelated tab or object out of sight. Nothing else is required.
2. Name the priority — Say what must receive attention before anything else. Let that count.
3. Park the rest — Put every competing demand on a short later list. Keep the next part outside.
4. Work one round — Stay with the selected move for one brief round. Do it once.
5. Mark the return — Leave one clear cue showing where to resume. Take a normal breath.

• Use a short timer to protect the chosen lane.
• Finish the current action before checking the queue.
• Park extra tasks where you can find them later.
• Make the next step physical and specific.

4. Make one request — Ask for one specific change or next action. Do it once.
5. Stop after the message — Do not weaken the point with a long defence. Take a normal breath.

• Describe behaviour instead of judging character.
• Kindness does not require a long explanation.

rituals.ritualText:
THE MAP GETS ONE VOTE

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

Reduce the pressure: understand before preparing your defence—with one small action.

1. Lower the defence — Let the first reaction pass before responding. Give it ten seconds.
2. Mirror the message — Use their key words without adding a judgement. One pass is enough.
3. Check the meaning — Ask if your summary is accurate. Return if attention slips.
4. Add your view — Share your perspective only after they feel heard. Choose safety over speed.
5. Choose the next step — Agree on one action, question, or pause. End at the first useful shift.

WIN

✓ The pressure eased enough; you heard the point before adding your reply in one short round.

TIPS

• For premature defence, change one visible thing at a time.
• Understanding does not mean automatic agreement.
• Let a correction land without defending yourself.
• Listen for meaning before preparing your reply.
• Keep your own view brief and specific.

MIND BEND

Understanding a message does not require agreeing with it. Lower the defence → Check the meaning → Choose the next step: The next choice matters more than the first reaction.

FORMULA FLOW

Lower the defence → Mirror the message → Check the meaning → Add your view → Choose the next step

SAFETY

PAUSE
Step away if the interaction is abusive, threatening, coercive, or unsafe. Use appropriate personal, workplace, legal, or professional support when needed.

rituals.name: THE HARBOUR DOESN'T DECIDE
rituals.challenge: You are scanning your body for danger
rituals.primary_trigger: You are scanning your body for danger
rituals.unique_game_move: Body-check amplification: Feel the floor → Drop the shoulders → Name three colours → Rate the wave → Choose the safe next
rituals.recognition_cue: Use this reset to lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.
rituals.situation: You are scanning your body for danger
rituals.immediate_need: Use this reset to lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.
rituals.match_reason: Body-check amplification · Use this reset to lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: Use this reset to lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Feel the floor — Press both feet down and notice the support. Give it ten seconds.
2. Drop the shoulders — Lower both shoulders and let the hands stay loose. One pass is enough.
3. Name three colours — Look around and name three colours you can see. Return if attention slips.
4. Rate the wave — Give the panic wave a number from zero to ten. Choose safety over speed.
5. Choose the safe next — Pick the least harmful action available now. End at the first useful shift.
rituals.win: ✓ You changed the next minute and stayed with the minute instead of the forecast.
rituals.winReward: ✓ You changed the next minute and stayed with the minute instead of the forecast.
rituals.tips:
• For body-check amplification, change one visible thing at a time.
• Seek urgent help if safety or medical risk is uncertain.
• Delay messages and decisions until the heat drops.
• Do not force a deep breath; soften the exhale.
• Use ordinary sights and sounds as anchors.

rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.ritualText:
THE HARBOUR DOESN'T DECIDE

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

Use this reset to lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.

1. Feel the floor — Press both feet down and notice the support. Give it ten seconds.
2. Drop the shoulders — Lower both shoulders and let the hands stay loose. One pass is enough.
3. Name three colours — Look around and name three colours you can see. Return if attention slips.
4. Rate the wave — Give the panic wave a number from zero to ten. Choose safety over speed.
5. Choose the safe next — Pick the least harmful action available now. End at the first useful shift.

WIN

✓ You changed the next minute and stayed with the minute instead of the forecast.

TIPS

• For body-check amplification, change one visible thing at a time.
• Seek urgent help if safety or medical risk is uncertain.
• Delay messages and decisions until the heat drops.
• Do not force a deep breath; soften the exhale.
• Use ordinary sights and sounds as anchors.

MIND BEND

A body alarm can feel urgent without predicting what happens next. Feel the floor → Name three colours → Choose the safe next: Action can begin before the feeling changes.

FORMULA FLOW

Feel the floor → Drop the shoulders → Name three colours → Rate the wave → Choose the safe next

SAFETY

PAUSE
If symptoms may reflect a medical emergency, severe withdrawal, immediate danger, self-harm risk, violence risk, or inability to stay safe, seek urgent professional or emergency help rather than continuing self-help exercises.
